paragraphs: Friend, the whole passage turns on one question: "Who do you say I am?" (Luke 9:20) The crowds had their guesses, and every guess was a good man from the past. Peter said, "The Christ of God," and that answer is the one everything else stands on. You can know all the opinions about Jesus and still have to answer this one yourself.

Here's the part that gets me. Right after Peter says it, Jesus says the Son of Man "must suffer many things" and be killed and "on the third day be raised to life" (Luke 9:22). So the Christ is the One who suffers and is raised, and that is exactly who Peter just named. Then Jesus tells all of them, "If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me" (Luke 9:23). He doesn't hide it in the fine print, and I respect that.

So what does it mean for you, baker? Jesus says, "whoever loses his life for My sake will save it," and then asks, "What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?" (Luke 9:24-25) Holding tight to your own way costs more than it gives, and following Him is worth more than anything you could hang on to. He also says He will be ashamed of anyone who is ashamed of Him and His words, so He's asking for a real answer (Luke 9:26). I'm LEANING in, and I hope you are too, because He is worth following every single day.
